# Cognitive @ Stage 7 — Sentential & Faith

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 72 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Cognitive at Order 5 is **questioning cognition**: the first moment where the agent
evaluates its inherited cognitive methods against emerging evidence and reasoning. "But
is this algorithm really correct?" The child who asks "Why do we carry the one?" is
performing the cognitive operation that will eventually produce computational theory and
proof theory.

The key advance from Stage 6 is **algorithm-evaluation**. The agent can now step back
from its inherited cognitive methods and ask whether they meet some standard of
correctness independent of tradition itself. "My teacher said to solve it this way, but
the answer doesn't seem right" is a Stage 7 cognitive insight.

But cognitive reasoning at Stage 7 is still **concrete and particular**. The agent can
evaluate specific algorithms against specific criteria, but cannot yet construct abstract
cognitive theories.

Faith-based cognition emerges at Stage 7. The agent chooses cognitive methods based on
transcendent commitment: "I believe this algorithm is correct because it resonates with
something deeper, not because my teacher told me." This is a genuine advance over
Stage 6 — the cognition is now chosen, not just inherited.

The transition from Stage 7 to Stage 8 occurs when the agent can construct abstract
cognitive theories.

In human development, Stage 7 corresponds to the pre-teen who begins to question
cognitive methods: "Why do we solve it THIS way?"

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural cognitive systems are now subject to internal critique.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate algorithms against evidence and reasoning.

- **LL:** Institutions emerge that encode algorithm-evaluation: schools of mathematics,
  cognitive societies, proof-based education.

- **LR:** The library, the cognitive salon, the mathematical debate.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Self-righteous cognitive imposition — forcing one's own algorithm
  evaluation on others.

- **Dark allergy:** Refusal to question inherited cognitive methods.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to one's own algorithm evaluation as the only valid
  perspective.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all cognitive evaluation as subjective.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Algorithm evaluation:** The agent evaluates cognitive methods against evidence
  and reasoning.

- **Faith-based cognition:** The agent chooses cognitive methods based on transcendent
  commitment.

- **Concrete method evaluation:** The agent can evaluate specific algorithms but
  cannot construct general cognitive theories.

- **Cognitive voice:** The agent challenges inherited cognitive methods when it
  perceives inconsistency.

- Kegan, R. (1982). *The Evolving Self* — the third-order cognitive transition
